properties_reviewed: Constructor fixes the canonical quote token, wrapper, treasury, and locked implementation.
Factory-only initialization and atomic clone creation prevent takeover and partial registration.
Prize escrow checks the exact token, token ID, sponsor, factory operator, final owner, and Active status.
Creation checks reserve, exclusive end time, maximum duration, contract presence, ERC-721 support, and known protocol destinations.
Registry identities remain consistent because any failed creation reverts counts, clones, and mappings.

properties_reviewed: One-time initialization rejects zero addresses and known protocol destinations.
Ticket ranges are positive, contiguous, disjoint, immutable, and bounded by uint128.
Ticket count cannot exceed total entries because each purchase buys at least one entry.
Purchases take entryCount * 1000000 USDC units and update complete range and liability state before receiver callbacks.
Transfer authorization follows inherited ERC-721 ownership and approvals; protocol-sink checks cover mints and transfers.
Ticket callbacks can transfer owned tickets but cannot reenter guarded purchase, refund, redemption, settlement, or withdrawal paths.
Only the immutable wrapper can call the randomness handler.
Only one accepted request and one authenticated, timely, correct-ID, single-word callback can resolve a sold raffle.
Request and callback deadline comparisons leave no overlap between accepted resolution and refund eligibility.
Random entry selection stays in [1,totalEntries]; the denominator is positive after requestDraw.
Historical ranges cannot prove a nonexistent winning ticket because winningEntry is positive in terminal winner states.
Settlement allocates the entire pot once; fee plus winner plus sponsor proceeds equals the prior unsettled pot.
At entry price 1000000, 500/10000 and 8000/10000 allocations produce exact integer USDC units.
Only the current owner can redeem or refund; transfer approvals alone do not confer a direct payout claim.
The winning ticket burns once before delivery, and any failed delivery reverts all redemption effects.
Refund batches reject empty, excessive, duplicate, nonexistent, or foreign-owned tickets and preserve aggregate liabilities.
Sponsor and treasury claims clear independently before token transfers and revert completely on transfer failure.
Sponsor prize release is restricted to CashWon or Refunding and occurs at most once.
Accounted quote liabilities exclude unsolicited donations and equal unsettled plus refund plus allocated claims.
Forced native balances cannot subsidize a successful draw because actual request price cannot exceed msg.value.
Factory initialization and prize callbacks cannot establish Active for a default uninitialized clone without the configured prize address.
Future-clone destinations can invalidate claim delivery, but the traced cases require the claimant to select the harmful recipient.
Prize transferability after escrow remains an external trust assumption; the native report preserves it as a lead.
